tools.name: structureSearch
tools.title: Structure Search
tools.fields: [path*, defaultExcludes?, entryType?, exclude?, extensions?, include?, …] | [operation:"files", path*, access?, accessedAt?, bytes?, defaultExcludes?, empty?, …]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode structureSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"tree","path":".","maxDepth":2}]}'
  octocode structureSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"files","path":".","include":["**/package.json"],"testCode":"exclude"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:
  tree   path
  files  path, operation

Each form's example: octocode schema structureSearch --view variants

Fields: octocode schema structureSearch

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and responsePagination may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.responsePagination: Reads on when next is present: preserve every row part and run next until none remains. Expired saved work fails explicitly.
output.responsePagination.next: Present while more of this request remains (absent on the last page): the rest of it, one call for the walks of the rows this response split; run unchanged. Rows keep their query's index.
output.responsePagination.replayed: Present (true) only on a page read back from saved output, without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.commitSha: The resolved source commit for this result.
output.errorCode: Machine code of the failure; errorClass says what to do next.
output.errorClass: The recovery the failure allows; the instructions name each class.
output.httpStatus: The provider's HTTP status, only when errorCode does not name it (a 5xx under server, an unmapped status under httpStatus, a status the provider read differently); a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 451 is errorCode alone.
output.retryable: On a transient row: whether a retry can succeed.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time a reused saved answer was observed, when the origin's own lifetime does not vouch for it (a disclosed reuse window, or a stale answer during a rate limit): the origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown. An answer within the origin's max-age is served as current, without observedAt.
output.redacted: Present (true) only when secret-shaped text in this row became [REDACTED-…] placeholders; the rest is verbatim.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Hints every empty or failed result row of this response states; those rows omit them. Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.next: Pagination and coverage continuations: the rest of this result (a paged response's walks ride responsePagination.next). Run each unchanged, even when pagination.hasMore is false. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.next.nextPage: The next page of this row's walk: run it unchanged until no nextPage is left.
output.next.unfiltered: The same read without classification: every unit the classified result left out, near misses included; not billed.
output.next.unfilteredUnknown: Only the units the classification left undecided (judged unsure, not judged or not judgeable), unfiltered, in one call; not billed.
output.next.nextCandidatePage: Judges the units this page left unjudged (its budget ran out or the provider could not answer); billed.
output.next.retry: The same call again after a transient failure; retryable says whether it can succeed.
output.next.restart: The request again from its first page, without its cursor: the source changed, so nothing the earlier pages showed remains valid.
output.pagination: Row-local pagination summary; for completeness see data.next, partialReasons and terminalLimit.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count, stated only for text windows: lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars. Absent for row lists: total counts the rows of the operation (commits, pullRequests, matches, tree entries) and offset is the first row of the page.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the text as served: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds, stated with a text window's unit; absent for row lists, where the rows listed are the page.
output.pagination.total: Size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.countScope: How much total counts: absent or complete, all of it; loaded, the part read so far; partial, what was readable; capped, up to the provider's result cap. Anything but complete makes total a floor.
output.pagination.hasMore: true: next.nextPage here or on the row, or responsePagination.next, reads the rest. false: this list or body is read to its end, not a guarantee that no other continuation exists.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row misses part of the requested scope for a reason pagination does not state; more pages show as hasMore with next.* or responsePagination.next, not as isPartial. Absent when partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope states it. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true, partialReasons is present, or pagination.countScope is capped, loaded or partial (total is then a floor); it states that once.
output.coverage.state: Absent when partial and stated by isPartial, partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope.
output.root: Stated once when the row's evidence lies outside the workspace (a clone, a materialized tree, another allowed root): the absolute root every path of the row is named from; root + "/" + path names the file, while the row's calls keep absolute paths. Absent: paths are workspace-relative.
output.selection: Coverage of a classified source view; counts are always visible when selection was requested.
output.selection.status: complete: every unit got an answer, unsure ones counted in unknownItems and near misses in relatedItems, so complete is not full recall; partial: some wait for next.nextCandidatePage or got no answer.
output.selection.unit: hits: each search hit has its own verdict. chunks: a read with no search, kept in whole declarations or line windows.
output.selection.totalItems: Every unit of the walk; each candidate page counts all pages so far.
output.selection.relatedItems: Hidden near-misses: judged related to a question but not direct evidence; next.unfiltered lists them; omitted when none.
output.selection.failures: Operational failures within unknownItems, distinct from model uncertainty; omitted when none.
output.selection.failures[].candidate: Zero-based candidate ordinal in selection scope, in source order.
output.selection.failures[].hints: Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.selection.reason: candidateBudget: Hits not judged yet, counted in unknownItems: next.nextCandidatePage judges them (billed). candidateIneligible: Candidates with no judgeable text were not judged; they stay in unknownItems. candidateEligibilityAndBudget: Both: some hits wait for next.nextCandidatePage, some had no judgeable text. classificationUnknown: The judge left some hits undecided; next.unfilteredUnknown lists them. classificationUnavailable: No classification provider: nothing was judged. noCandidates: Nothing to judge: the search or read held no hits. unreadSections: The read held no entry of the kind this tool judges; warnings name the sections that may hold them. Not absence. Any other value: the errorCode that stopped judging.
output.selection.usage: Fresh usage for this classification call; token totals exclude replay and may be incomplete when unknownUsageCalls is nonzero.
output.selection.usage.remainingInputTokensEsti: Rough input tokens the rest of this walk would bill, at this page's rate.
output.selection.usage.models: Distinct models that supplied validated answers.
output.selection.usage.replayed: true: this page repeats an earlier judgment; nothing was billed again.
output.selection.usage.requestsPlanned: First-round requests, planned before any was sent.
output.selection.usage.requestsCeiling: Most requests this page can send: the first round plus every re-ask and split a refusal or missing answer can add.
output.files[].dir: Named like a row path (workspace-relative, or from root when the row states one); entry path = dir + "/" + name.
output.files[].files[]: Entry "<name>[/][ (<fields>)]": "/" marks a directory, "." the listed dir itself. Fields, in order: bytes (every non-directory), "symlink"; details: lines, modified (ISO 8601 UTC, seconds); the last " (" of an entry ending in ")" opens them.
output.summary: Stated only on a paged or partial listing; a listing without pagination is complete: count its entries. Totals of the entries pagination.total counts, never one page's share: the whole listing, or with countScope loaded, the rows this window loaded. fileCount (matching non-directory entries, symlinks included); dirCount (matching directory entries; a group header that only holds matched files is not counted); bytes when known.
output.skippedPaths: What the walk skipped, not an inventory of unwalked descendants; includeIgnored, includeHidden and defaultExcludes:false lift ignored, hidden and default-excluded; ignored-default-excluded: a path both ignored and default-excluded, one entry that needs both flags lifted. octocode-artifact: Octocode's own store under the workspace (.octocode/graph), skipped whatever the flags; a path inside it searches it. withheld: the path policy (no flag lifts it; path is the directory holding the withheld files, whose names are never shown; reason is the rule); unreadable: read errors. unparsed: a file the walk passed over because no grammar parses its name (reason: its file type, if it has one); each is its own entry, never a count, so paging reaches every file the skipped-files warning counts; parserGlobs maps its name to a grammar. sampled: the walk ended before every skipped path was seen; counts are floors. Written only when true; absent means every skipped path is listed.
output.skippedPaths.entries[].count: Skipped paths of this cause and rule; path is the deepest directory holding them all. Lifting the cause walks each.
output.skippedPaths.entries[].reason: The rule that skipped it; default-excluded: the pattern or directory name, e.g. *.min.js, node_modules/.
output.testCodeExcluded.files: Files left out (listings: entries left out). A file a module root mounts as test code by #[path] is left out unread; one another module mounts counts once a hit or listing reaches it.
output.testCodeExcluded.lines: Hit lines left out inside searched files.
output.filesScanned: Files the scan read: coverage, never a result count.
output.clipped: The walk stopped at its window or time budget before every entry was listed; next reads the rest.
output.atLeast: Clipped early: at least this many entries match (this window's start plus its rows plus one).
output.totalAvailable: Clipped after counting: entries matching in all.
output.window: The absolute bounds (RFC 3339 UTC) a duration in modifiedAt or accessedAt resolved to, once for this query.
output.results[].status: Absent: evidence. empty: nothing in the asked scope matched; the row's other facts still hold. error: errorCode says why. outOfRange: a page past the end; pagination.total states the size (next.restart).
output.results[].rowPart: This row spans response pages; concatenate its parts in order.
output.results[].rowPart.continues: The innermost array element this part continues; pointer indexes are the joined row's, and each element on the pointer path also continues.
output.results[].rowPart.continues.array: JSON pointer of the array this part resumes.
output.results[].rowPart.text: JSON pointer, in the joined row's indexes, of the string this part continues: append this part's value there to the previous part's.
output.shared.data: Facts every result row of this response states alike; those rows omit them. A row reads a field it lacks from its nearest holder, then its data, then here, then the request.
output.shared.data.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true, partialReasons is present, or pagination.countScope is capped, loaded or partial (total is then a floor); it states that once.
output.related: Optional fresh calls, each merging the rows' one-query related calls of one tool; run unchanged.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.description:
<when>Questions about files, not text: largest, longest, newest, empty, by name, extension, size or date, a half-known path, the layout.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"files","path":".","entryType":"file","sort":{"by":"bytes","order":"desc"},"limit":1}]}

path.description: tree requires a directory.

view.description: paths: names only (a size, line or date sort adds its one value), fastest; directories end in /. details: adds "(bytes, lines, modified ISO)" to each entry, reading each listed file to count lines.

entryType.description: Symlinks match neither; omit to list them.

include.description: Globs relative to path: "*.rs" at any depth, "src/*.rs" only in src; a substring needs "*name*".

exclude.description: Globs to skip, on top of defaultExcludes and testCode.

limit.description: Omit: the automatic page window (a default size) per row; limit only shrinks it.

operation.description: tree: the layout under a directory; files: entries that pass the filters, sortable.

maxDepth.description: tree: Omit: 1. files: Omit: every level.

reasoning.description: Evidence so far; why this query decides.

testCode.description: Test files and dirs by convention, plus Rust #[cfg(test)] items. Omit: include.

nameRegex.description: Case-sensitive regex on the entry's name, not its path.

empty.description: true: only empty entries; false: only non-empty.

modifiedAt.description: Modified within ISO bounds (Z or an offset) or durations back from now (-P1D).

bytes.description: Never matches a directory or link.

permissions.description: Exact octal mode ("755" does not match a 4755 file). Refused on Windows.

sort.description: Ranks the whole scope, then pages; a walk over its time budget pauses with no rows: next resumes. Entries lacking the key rank last. totalLines reads every file.

tools.name: astSearch
tools.title: AST Search
tools.fields: [operation:"match", path*, rule*, defaultExcludes?, exclude?, include?, includeCaptures?, …] | [operation:"match", path*, rule*, view*, defaultExcludes?, exclude?, include?, …] | [operation:"syntaxTree", path*, includeProvenance?, line?, mainGoal?, namedOnly?, parser?, …] | [operation:"symbols", path*, defaultExcludes?, exclude?, includeHidden?, includeIgnored?, includeProvenance?, …]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode astSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"match","path":"src","parser":"typescript","rule":{"pattern":"eval($X)"}}]}'
  octocode astSearch '{
    "queries": [{"operation":"match","path":"src","rule":{"kind":"class_declaration"},"view":"files","testCode":"exclude"}]
  }'
  octocode astSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"syntaxTree","path":"src/index.ts"}]}'
  octocode astSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"symbols","path":"src","symbolFilter":{"terms":["main"],"mode":"exact"}}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:

output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.name: astSearch
query.description:
<when>Code shape, not spelling (localSearch): calls, imports, inheritance, containment (a function, closure or loop whose body holds a call), declarations, a syntaxTree. operation symbols with symbolFilter finds a declaration cheaper than lspSearch workspaceSymbol.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"match","path":"src","rule":{"any":[{"kind":"function_declaration"},{"kind":"arrow_function"}],"has":{"pattern":"eval($X)","stopBy":"end"}}}]}
Columns count the shown text, after redaction. One file's outline: localFetch symbols. Empty: check filesScanned, diagnostics and parseAssessment.

querySchema.description: operation: syntaxTree takes only path, parser, includeProvenance, line, namedOnly, mainGoal, reasoning. For scope, include, maxDepth, sort, view, includeCaptures: only with operation: match. For line, namedOnly: only with operation: syntaxTree. For symbolFilter, symbolKinds: only with operation: symbols.

exclude.description: Globs to skip, on top of defaultExcludes and testCode.

defaultExcludes.description: false: also walk build, dependency and cache dirs (Git-unignored ones always; credential dirs never).

testCode.description: Test files and dirs by convention, plus Rust #[cfg(test)] items. Omit: include.

parser.description: On a directory, match reads only this grammar's extensions. A build may lack optional grammars. symbols: Forces this grammar on a file path; on a directory, map globs with parserGlobs.

limit.description: Rows: matches, files or top-level declarations; members ride along. Omit: the automatic page window (a default size) per row; limit only shrinks it.

operation.description: match: Nodes the rule fits. syntaxTree: One file's node kinds, to write a rule. symbols: Declarations by name and kind.

scope.description: One file only; UTF-16 columns, exclusive end.

include.description: Globs relative to path: "*.rs" at any depth, "src/*.rs" only in src; a substring needs "*name*".

sort.description: Orders the files.

rule.description: pattern: code with metavariables ($X one node, $$$ARGS zero or more); {context,selector} for a fragment. A declaration pattern requires only what it spells; calls and expressions keep every part; exclude an unsaid part with not. regex: tests a node's whole text, so alone it matches every enclosing node; pair it with kind or field. kind: as syntaxTree prints it, or a CSS-like selector. has, inside: direct children, direct parent; stopBy:"end" reaches any depth. nthChild: integer or An+B. range: 1-based. Required with operation: match.

stopBy.description: stopBy goes inside has, inside, precedes or follows; field only in has or inside. Neither on the rule.

view.description: files: a row per matching file; countMatches: with its match count.

includeCaptures.description: true: each match whole, each capture in metavarRanges; add include to read one file. Without it a long match is cut, ending with …, and matches carry line (and endLine), no column. Only with view: content.

includeProvenance.description: For exact-byte claims: adds byte ranges, origins and digests. Derived or unmapped evidence cannot prove raw quotes.

reasoning.description: Evidence so far; why this query decides.

line.description: Start at the smallest node covering it.

symbolFilter.description: exactFirst drops substring matches when an exact name exists.

caseMode.description: smart: an uppercase letter makes that pattern case-sensitive.

symbolKinds.description: class, constant, constructor, enum, enumMember, function, impl, interface, label, macro, method, module, namespace, property, struct, symbol, trait, type, variable. Rust: fn in impl is method; const and static are constant.

stopBy.description: Default: the immediate neighbor; "end": to the file edge, or a rule.

tools.name: localFetch
tools.title: Local Fetch Content
tools.fields: [view?:"content", path*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?] | [view?:"content", path*, ranges*, block?, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?] | [view?:"content", matchString*, path*, block?, caseMode?, contextLines?, limit?, …] | [view:"compact", path*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?] | [view:"compact", path*, ranges*, block?, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?] | [view:"symbols", path*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts"}]}'
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","ranges":[{"startLine":1,"endLine":30}]}]}'
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","matchString":["function"]}]}'
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","view":"compact"}]}'
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","view":"compact","ranges":[{"startLine":1,"endLine":30}]}]}'
  octocode localFetch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","view":"symbols"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:
  content         path
  ranges          path, ranges
  matches         path, matchString
  compact         path, view
  compact:ranges  path, view, ranges
  symbols         path, view

Each form's example: octocode schema localFetch --view variants

Fields: octocode schema localFetch

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and responsePagination may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.responsePagination: Reads on when next is present: preserve every row part and run next until none remains. Expired saved work fails explicitly.
output.responsePagination.next: Present while more of this request remains (absent on the last page): the rest of it, one call for the walks of the rows this response split; run unchanged. Rows keep their query's index.
output.responsePagination.replayed: Present (true) only on a page read back from saved output, without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.httpStatus: The provider's HTTP status, only when errorCode does not name it (a 5xx under server, an unmapped status under httpStatus, a status the provider read differently); a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 451 is errorCode alone.
output.retryable: On a transient row: whether a retry can succeed.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time a reused saved answer was observed, when the origin's own lifetime does not vouch for it (a disclosed reuse window, or a stale answer during a rate limit): the origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown. An answer within the origin's max-age is served as current, without observedAt.
output.redacted: Present (true) only when secret-shaped text in this row became [REDACTED-…] placeholders; the rest is verbatim.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Hints every empty or failed result row of this response states; those rows omit them. Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.next: Pagination and coverage continuations: the rest of this result (a paged response's walks ride responsePagination.next). Run each unchanged, even when pagination.hasMore is false. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.next.nextPage: The next page of this row's walk: run it unchanged until no nextPage is left.
output.next.unfiltered: The same read without classification: every unit the classified result left out, near misses included; not billed.
output.next.unfilteredUnknown: Only the units the classification left undecided (judged unsure, not judged or not judgeable), unfiltered, in one call; not billed.
output.next.nextCandidatePage: Judges the units this page left unjudged (its budget ran out or the provider could not answer); billed.
output.next.retry: The same call again after a transient failure; retryable says whether it can succeed.
output.next.restart: The request again from its first page, without its cursor: the source changed, so nothing the earlier pages showed remains valid.
output.pagination: Row-local pagination summary; for completeness see data.next, partialReasons and terminalLimit.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count, stated only for text windows: lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars. Absent for row lists: total counts the rows of the operation (commits, pullRequests, matches, tree entries) and offset is the first row of the page.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the text as served: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds, stated with a text window's unit; absent for row lists, where the rows listed are the page.
output.pagination.total: Size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.countScope: How much total counts: absent or complete, all of it; loaded, the part read so far; partial, what was readable; capped, up to the provider's result cap. Anything but complete makes total a floor.
output.pagination.hasMore: true: next.nextPage here or on the row, or responsePagination.next, reads the rest. false: this list or body is read to its end, not a guarantee that no other continuation exists.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row misses part of the requested scope for a reason pagination does not state; more pages show as hasMore with next.* or responsePagination.next, not as isPartial. Absent when partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope states it. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true, partialReasons is present, or pagination.countScope is capped, loaded or partial (total is then a floor); it states that once.
output.coverage.state: Absent when partial and stated by isPartial, partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope.
output.root: Stated once when the row's evidence lies outside the workspace (a clone, a materialized tree, another allowed root): the absolute root every path of the row is named from; root + "/" + path names the file, while the row's calls keep absolute paths. Absent: paths are workspace-relative.
output.selection: Coverage of a classified source view; counts are always visible when selection was requested.
output.selection.status: complete: every unit got an answer, unsure ones counted in unknownItems and near misses in relatedItems, so complete is not full recall; partial: some wait for next.nextCandidatePage or got no answer.
output.selection.unit: hits: each search hit has its own verdict. chunks: a read with no search, kept in whole declarations or line windows.
output.selection.totalItems: Every unit of the walk; each candidate page counts all pages so far.
output.selection.relatedItems: Hidden near-misses: judged related to a question but not direct evidence; next.unfiltered lists them; omitted when none.
output.selection.failures: Operational failures within unknownItems, distinct from model uncertainty; omitted when none.
output.selection.failures[].candidate: Zero-based candidate ordinal in selection scope, in source order.
output.selection.failures[].hints: Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.selection.reason: candidateBudget: Hits not judged yet, counted in unknownItems: next.nextCandidatePage judges them (billed). candidateIneligible: Candidates with no judgeable text were not judged; they stay in unknownItems. candidateEligibilityAndBudget: Both: some hits wait for next.nextCandidatePage, some had no judgeable text. classificationUnknown: The judge left some hits undecided; next.unfilteredUnknown lists them. classificationUnavailable: No classification provider: nothing was judged. noCandidates: Nothing to judge: the search or read held no hits. unreadSections: The read held no entry of the kind this tool judges; warnings name the sections that may hold them. Not absence. Any other value: the errorCode that stopped judging.
output.selection.usage: Fresh usage for this classification call; token totals exclude replay and may be incomplete when unknownUsageCalls is nonzero.
output.selection.usage.remainingInputTokensEsti: Rough input tokens the rest of this walk would bill, at this page's rate.
output.selection.usage.models: Distinct models that supplied validated answers.
output.selection.usage.replayed: true: this page repeats an earlier judgment; nothing was billed again.
output.selection.usage.requestsPlanned: First-round requests, planned before any was sent.
output.selection.usage.requestsCeiling: Most requests this page can send: the first round plus every re-ask and split a refusal or missing answer can add.
output.symlinkTarget: Repository symlink: the path it points to; withholding judged that path.
output.totalLines: Lines in the whole file; stated on a read's first page.
output.selectedMatchCount: Matches matchString selects in the whole read, stated on its first page; under classification, the matches this page kept, on every page.
output.matchedLines: Source lines in this page hit by matchString; [] means this page contains no hit lines. Absent with matchString: every line this page shows is a hit.
output.matchKeys: JSON or TOML file: each hit line's key path, e.g. {"221":"devDependencies.vite"}; [i] is an array item.
output.startLine: First source line shown; omitted when one sourceLineRanges span states it.
output.matchRanges: matchString hit spans on this page.
output.viewFallback: The view applied instead of the requested view, and why.
output.blocks: Declarations a block:true match read widened hits to (name line, last line); stated on a read's first page.
output.results[].status: Absent: evidence. empty: nothing in the asked scope matched; the row's other facts still hold. error: errorCode says why. outOfRange: a page past the end; pagination.total states the size (next.restart).
output.results[].rowPart: This row spans response pages; concatenate its parts in order.
output.results[].rowPart.continues: The innermost array element this part continues; pointer indexes are the joined row's, and each element on the pointer path also continues.
output.results[].rowPart.continues.array: JSON pointer of the array this part resumes.
output.results[].rowPart.text: JSON pointer, in the joined row's indexes, of the string this part continues: append this part's value there to the previous part's.
output.shared.data: Facts every result row of this response states alike; those rows omit them. A row reads a field it lacks from its nearest holder, then its data, then here, then the request.
output.shared.data.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true, partialReasons is present, or pagination.countScope is capped, loaded or partial (total is then a floor); it states that once.
output.related: Optional fresh calls, each merging the rows' one-query related calls of one tool; run unchanged.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.description:
<when>Read part of a known file: a named function, a range or the outline, with no search first. Unknown path: structureSearch or localSearch. A named function: matchString+block; view:"compact" takes only the whole file or ranges.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","matchString":["function run"],"block":true}]}
totalLines is the file length; pagination counts the view's source rows; an uncounted -- row marks a gap between windows in a page. matchString and results see redacted source (known secret formats and quoted values anywhere, bare KEY=value only in config files); such rows carry redacted: true.

querySchema.description: For ranges, block: never with view: symbols. For regexEngine, caseMode, wholeWord, contextLines: needs matchString.

limit.description: Rows: source lines; matchedLines lists this page's hits only. Omit: as many as responseChars holds.

view.description: compact: Safe comment/whitespace removal; read, do not quote. symbols: Rows: line or start-end, tab, the declaration's first line; doc comments sit above: quote from the line above. viewFallback names the view served.

reasoning.description: Evidence so far; why this query decides.

ranges.description: Inclusive. Read in file order; overlapping or adjacent ranges merge. Past the file end clips with a warning. Omit ranges and matchString: whole file, paged.

block.description: Whole enclosing declaration or Markdown section; for a signature only, use contextLines.

matchString.description: ORed; literal unless regexEngine is set. With ranges, only matches inside them count. Only with view: content.

caseMode.description: smart: an uppercase letter makes that pattern case-sensitive.

contextLines.description: Lines around each match.

tools.fields: [operation?:"definition"|"typeDefinition"|"implementation", line*, path*, symbolName*, contextLines?, limit?, mainGoal?, …] | [operation?:"definition"|"typeDefinition"|"implementation", line*, path*, symbolName*, view*, limit?, mainGoal?, …] | [operation:"references", line*, path*, symbolName*, contextLines?, includeDeclaration?, limit?, …] | [operation:"references", line*, path*, symbolName*, view*, includeDeclaration?, limit?, …] | [operation:"callers", line*, path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, mainGoal?, …] | [operation:"callees"|"supertypes", line*, path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, mainGoal?, …] | [operation:"subtypes", line*, path*, symbolName*, depth?, limit?, mainGoal?, …] | [operation:"hover", line*, path*, symbolName*, limit?, mainGoal?, occurrence?, …] | [operation:"documentSymbols"|"diagnostic", path*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?, workspaceRoot?] | [operation:"workspaceSymbol", path*, symbolFuzzy*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?, workspaceRoot?] | [operation:"workspaceSymbol", symbolFuzzy*, workspaceRoot*, limit?, mainGoal?, reasoning?]
tools.help:
Examples:
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10,"view":"files"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"references","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{
    "queries": [{"operation":"references","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10,"view":"files","testCode":"exclude"}]
  }'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"callers","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"callees","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"subtypes","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"Runner","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"hover","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"path":"src/index.ts","operation":"documentSymbols"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"workspaceSymbol","path":"src/index.ts","symbolFuzzy":"run"}]}'
  octocode lspSearch '{"queries":[{"operation":"workspaceSymbol","workspaceRoot":".","symbolFuzzy":"run"}]}'

Input: {"queries":[…]} for fresh calls, optionally with "responseChars" (the size of each response page; the rest pages, nothing dropped; local walk rows still page at the automatic window); copy {"cursor":"…"} from a continuation.
Up to 5 queries per call.

Required fields, by operation:
  definition, typeDefinition, implementation              path, symbolName, line
  definition, typeDefinition, implementation (with view)  path, symbolName, line, view
  references                                              path, symbolName, line, operation
  references (with view)                                  path, symbolName, line, operation, view
  callers                                                 path, symbolName, line, operation
  callees, supertypes                                     path, symbolName, line, operation
  subtypes                                                path, symbolName, line, operation
  hover                                                   path, symbolName, line, operation
  documentSymbols, diagnostic                             path, operation
  workspaceSymbol                                         operation, symbolFuzzy, path
  workspaceSymbol                                         workspaceRoot, operation, symbolFuzzy

Each form's example: octocode schema lspSearch --view variants

Fields: octocode schema lspSearch

output.warnings: Notes for the whole response; each applies to every row.
output.oversized: This response holds an indivisible value longer than responseChars; nothing is cut. Fixed envelope parts, repeated context and responsePagination may exceed the target without this flag. Per-call metadata (rateLimit, clientWaits, observedAt) and rejected queries are not counted.
output.responsePagination: Reads on when next is present: preserve every row part and run next until none remains. Expired saved work fails explicitly.
output.responsePagination.next: Present while more of this request remains (absent on the last page): the rest of it, one call for the walks of the rows this response split; run unchanged. Rows keep their query's index.
output.responsePagination.replayed: Present (true) only on a page read back from saved output, without acquisition or inference; any usage in the output is historical.
output.commitSha: The resolved source commit for this result.
output.errorCode: Machine code of the failure; errorClass says what to do next.
output.errorClass: The recovery the failure allows; the instructions name each class.
output.httpStatus: The provider's HTTP status, only when errorCode does not name it (a 5xx under server, an unmapped status under httpStatus, a status the provider read differently); a 401, 403, 404, 429 or 451 is errorCode alone.
output.retryable: On a transient row: whether a retry can succeed.
output.ssoUrl: GitHub SAML SSO authorization URL (x-github-sso) for a 403 whose token must be authorized for the org; open it, then retry.
output.clientWaits: Waits this row spent on the client before its provider requests, by kind: latency the provider did not cause.
output.observedAt: ISO time a reused saved answer was observed, when the origin's own lifetime does not vouch for it (a disclosed reuse window, or a stale answer during a rate limit): the origin was not asked again, so later changes are not shown. An answer within the origin's max-age is served as current, without observedAt.
output.redacted: Present (true) only when secret-shaped text in this row became [REDACTED-…] placeholders; the rest is verbatim.
output.rateLimit: The provider's rate limit behind a failure: when a retry can run.
output.rateLimit.resource: The provider's limit bucket, e.g. core or search.
output.hints: Hints every empty or failed result row of this response states; those rows omit them. Optional guidance for empty results or errors; evidence and coverage disclosures go in warnings, executable follow-ups in objects. Related calls never complete a partial result.
output.next: Pagination and coverage continuations: the rest of this result (a paged response's walks ride responsePagination.next). Run each unchanged, even when pagination.hasMore is false. Only this field, never hints, may satisfy isPartial.
output.next.nextPage: The next page of this row's walk: run it unchanged until no nextPage is left.
output.next.nextImporterWindow: Verifies the next window of candidate importer files (the TS/JS importer scan); offered on each of this window's location pages, so every candidate is verified in exactly one window.
output.next.continueWalk: Resumes a hierarchy walk that stopped at its node cap or fan-out, re-anchored on a parent whose children were dropped; one per such parent (continueWalk, continueWalk2, …).
output.next.nextCandidatePage: Judges the units this page left unjudged (its budget ran out or the provider could not answer); billed.
output.next.readDeclaration: Reads the rest of a declaration body this row clipped (localFetch); one per clipped body (readDeclaration, readDeclaration2, …).
output.next.sourceDefinition: Reads the source declaration a definition in a package's build output (a tsconfig outDir .d.ts) was compiled from, mapped through that tsconfig's rootDir and outDir.
output.next.retry: The same call again after a transient failure; retryable says whether it can succeed.
output.next.restart: The request again from its first page, without its cursor: the source changed, so nothing the earlier pages showed remains valid.
output.pagination: Row-local pagination summary; for completeness see data.next, partialReasons and terminalLimit.
output.pagination.unit: What offset, length and total count, stated only for text windows: lines (localSearch hit rows: a matched line, or each hit window of a long line; a body's lines), bytes or chars. Absent for row lists: total counts the rows of the operation (commits, pullRequests, matches, tree entries) and offset is the first row of the page.
output.pagination.offset: Where this page starts in unit, from 0. A bytes window counts the text as served: decoded (a BOM dropped, UTF-16 as UTF-8), each redaction placeholder as the bytes it shows, so it can differ from the file's bytes.
output.pagination.length: How many units this page holds, stated with a text window's unit; absent for row lists, where the rows listed are the page.
output.pagination.total: Size of the whole list or body in unit; absent when unknown. A read counts what it selects (its ranges, matches or transformed view), not the file: data.totalLines counts the file, and a lines window states total only when it differs.
output.pagination.countScope: How much total counts: absent or complete, all of it; loaded, the part read so far; partial, what was readable; capped, up to the provider's result cap. Anything but complete makes total a floor.
output.pagination.hasMore: true: next.nextPage here or on the row, or responsePagination.next, reads the rest. false: this list or body is read to its end, not a guarantee that no other continuation exists.
output.pagination.oversized: A bytes or chars window shows an indivisible redaction marker whole: its text is wider than length, cut short of the marker, or empty when the marker belongs to the next window. Offsets stay nominal; walking on still reads every unit once.
output.isPartial: True when this row misses part of the requested scope for a reason pagination does not state; more pages show as hasMore with next.* or responsePagination.next, not as isPartial. Absent when partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope states it. Inspect next, partialReasons, warnings and terminalLimit.
output.terminalLimit: True when a provider or runtime limit leaves part of the requested scope unreachable by any call; report that scope. A next call still reads the rest, so keep walking.
output.partialReasons: Machine-readable reasons this row has incomplete coverage.
output.coverage: complete covers the stated scope; partial leaves evidence unread, so absence is unproven; error: nothing was judged. reason explains a gap; next.* may offer drill-downs even when complete. A page is partial when isPartial is true, partialReasons is present, or pagination.countScope is capped, loaded or partial (total is then a floor); it states that once.
output.coverage.state: Absent when partial and stated by isPartial, partialReasons or an incomplete pagination countScope.
output.coverage.textOnlyFiles: Files under the search scope, within the declaration's reach, that spell the name as a word in a way that could answer the question but are not in the answer; 0 clears file-level partial reasons.
output.coverage.outOfReachFiles: Files the text check read that spell the name outside the declaration's reach (its visibility, its crate, or a local binding's scope): not missed sites, not partial.
output.coverage.unreadOutOfReach: Files of the scope outside the declaration's reach (a Rust module, crate or local binding) that the text check did not read: they cannot reference it, so they are not missed sites and the row is not partial. Counted apart from outOfReachFiles.
output.coverage.importerScan: The TS/JS importer scan that adds files the server did not report, stated when it did not end clean: capped, later importer windows remain (next.nextImporterWindow); failed, cross-file results unverified. Absent: every candidate verified, or no scan ran.
output.coverage.verifiedImporterFiles: Importer files the scan verified beyond the server's answer; present only above 0 (absent: it added none, not that nothing was verified).
output.coverage.tooLargeFiles: Importer candidates that spell the name but are larger than a language server is sent (a vendored bundle): counted instead of verified, not a failed scan; the related localSearch reads them.
output.coverage.packageImporters: TS/JS importer files that bind the name through the anchor package's build output (its tsconfig outDir .d.ts) that the scan could not map back to this source declaration: unverified, so the row is partial (importUnresolved); the related localSearch reads them.
output.coverage.cfgGatedFiles: Rust files missing from the answer that use the name in code under a cfg gate the analyzed configuration leaves out (partialReasons cfgGatedFiles).
output.coverage.importerScanRoot: The request's workspaceRoot bounded the scan below the repository: importers outside it went unscanned.
output.root: Stated once when the row's evidence lies outside the workspace (a clone, a materialized tree, another allowed root): the absolute root every path of the row is named from; root + "/" + path names the file, while the row's calls keep absolute paths. Absent: paths are workspace-relative.
output.sourceEvidence: Exact descriptor closure for this response fragment's origins. Each origin and descriptor stays atomic; projection limits fail explicitly.
output.sourceEvidence.snapshots[]: Original file bytes. latin1 is 8-bit text read one character per byte; lossy is UTF-8 with stray bytes, each run read as U+FFFD. Identity commits to the authorized source occurrence and raw digest, not the displayed path alone.
output.sourceEvidence.representations[]: UTF-8 parser representation. sourceIds is its unique raw-source closure, empty for decoded-only input. Identity includes derivation, not just content.
output.sourceEvidence.representations[].produce: Registered producer identity and implementation version.
output.sourceEvidence.units[]: Ordered analyzed regions in the identified representation. Empty input uses [0,0]; excluded gaps are not analyzed source.
output.sourceEvidence.units[].adapter: Registered producer identity and implementation version.
output.sourceEvidence.units[].regions[]: Half-open byte range. Its owning field identifies the representation; endpoints must be ordered.
output.testCodeExcluded.files: Files left out (listings: entries left out). A file a module root mounts as test code by #[path] is left out unread; one another module mounts counts once a hit or listing reaches it.
output.testCodeExcluded.lines: Hit lines left out inside searched files.
output.path: The queried file or directory, named as a row path (from root when stated).
output.lsp.level: Which engine answered: ide the editor's providers through the Octocode extension; server a language server Octocode started; syntax tree-sitter facts matched by name (unverified); text no engine, follow the leads.
output.lsp.fellBackFrom: The better engine that did not answer, and why.
output.lsp.ide: The editor whose providers answered at level ide.
output.lsp.source: How a fallback request was answered: heritage or implementation the server through heritage clauses or textDocument/implementation; native-graph-facts a source scan (unverified).
output.lsp.analysisContext: Observed diagnostic and configuration context; neither configuration presence nor no reported errors proves usable compilation or complete indexing.
output.lsp.analysisContext.diagnostics: unavailable: no diagnostics report for the answered document version arrived, so errors are not ruled out; noErrorsReported: the report listed none; errors: errorCount counts them.
output.resolvedSymbol: Present only when the anchor was found elsewhere than requested (another line or file, or a line spelling the name more than once): cite foundAtLine and path.
output.matchCount: References in this answer (an importer window past the first counts its own rows).
output.matchedFiles: Files holding a hit in this answer.
output.reason: Absent when category says it all.

output.results[].rowPart.continues: The innermost array element this part continues; pointer indexes are the joined row's, and each element on the pointer path also continues.
output.results[].rowPart.continues.array: JSON pointer of the array this part resumes.

output.shared.data: Facts every result row of this response states alike; those rows omit them. A row reads a field it lacks from its nearest holder, then its data, then here, then the request.

output.related: Optional fresh calls, each merging the rows' one-query related calls of one tool; run unchanged.
output.error: Why the whole call was rejected.

query.name: lspSearch
query.description:
<when>What a name resolves to or who uses it: definitions, references, implementations, callers, callees, type hierarchies, hover types, diagnostics, document symbols, workspaceSymbol. Finds uses outside the searched path; references view:files first.</when>
Example: {"queries":[{"operation":"callers","path":"src/index.ts","symbolName":"run","line":10}]}
The first call for a language and project may wait seconds while its server starts and loads it; later calls reuse it. Fetched code (ghCloneRepo if listed, ghStructure materialize) starts no server unless settings allow; on errorCode policy use localSearch or astSearch.
references rows: role is declaration, call, import or reference. callers, callees: a row per symbol; sites lists its call lines.
TS/JS coverage.importerScan capped: also take next.nextImporterWindow; failed: cross-file results unverified. Gitignored and hidden files are outside the text and importer scans, as in localSearch.
No lsp field: the server reported no errors. Not proof: empty while lsp.analysisContext reports errors; workspaceSymbol (no page completes it: confirm with localSearch); rows matched by name, not by the server (lsp.level syntax or text, source native-graph-facts). source recovered*: a site checked at its line; kind file: an unnamed caller.

querySchema.description: For symbolName, line: required with operation: definition, typeDefinition, implementation, references, callers, callees, supertypes, subtypes, hover. For symbolName, line, occurrence: never with operation: documentSymbols, diagnostic, workspaceSymbol. For view, contextLines: only with operation: definition, typeDefinition, implementation, references.

workspaceRoot.description: Omit to infer it. A narrower root narrows importer scans.

limit.description: Rows: locations, hierarchy edges, symbols or diagnostics. Omit: the automatic page window (a default size) per row; limit only shrinks it.

path.description: Anchor file. workspaceSymbol: a file in the project to search (no file known: find one with localSearch for the name, or structureSearch); a directory or workspaceRoot searches only one project, which an empty answer's hint names. Required except with operation: workspaceSymbol.

symbolName.description: The identifier at line, as written.

line.description: 1-based line where symbolName appears, such as a search hit's.

occurrence.description: 0-based: which identifier spelled symbolName on line, left to right.

operation.description: workspaceSymbol needs one of: path, workspaceRoot. workspaceSymbol with path: A file path searches its project. workspaceSymbol: With only workspaceRoot, the server searches one project it chooses: partial; prefer path.

contextLines.description: Omit: the declaration page (next.readDeclaration pages the rest). Only with view: content.

reasoning.description: Evidence so far; why this query decides.

includeDeclaration.description: false: drop the declaration row. Only with operation: references.

testCode.description: Test files and dirs by convention, plus Rust #[cfg(test)] items. Omit: include. Sites left out count in testCodeExcluded. Only with operation: references, callers.

depth.description: Only with operation: callers, callees, supertypes, subtypes.

symbolFuzzy.description: Fuzzy substring. Required with operation: workspaceSymbol.
